Text: Bank of America’s Merrill Lynch unit will pay $39 million to settle a class-action lawsuit alleging that it paid brokerage clients near-zero interest rates instead of market rates on unused cash in retirement accounts. The preliminary settlement was filed in Manhattan federal court and requires approval from Judge Valerie Caproni. The settlement covers Merrill Edge online account holders between Dec. 15, 2016 and March 15, 2020, who allegedly received rates of 0.05%-0.14%, while some competitors paid around 2%. Merrill Lynch denied wrongdoing. In a separate case, Judge Margaret Garnett ruled that most of another class action covering retirement and non-retirement accounts can proceed. Similar lawsuits have targeted major banks and brokers over alleged cash-sweep practices that moved client funds into low-interest accounts. Merrill also agreed in January 2025 to pay $25 million to settle related SEC claims without admitting wrongdoing. $BAC

Text: U.S. regulators announced a historic $1.21 billion enforcement action against Bank of America over systemic failures in its anti-money-laundering and sanctions compliance programs. Text: Bank of America is preparing to raise $8 billion through an unusual investment-grade bond offering on Friday, returning to the debt market for the first time since April despite a turbulent week for credit markets.
